skill.name: research-storage
skill.description: Defines storage paths, naming rules, lookup strategy, and Markdown templates for cached dokhak research files.
skill.summary: Organize cached dokhak research with consistent paths, lookup rules, and file templates.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malicious intent, command execution, obfuscation, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline path formatting, documentation templates, and example Claude tool calls for Read, Write, and Glob.

static_findings.snippet: > Glob does NOT return directories. All patterns MUST end with a filename (e.g., `/research.md`).
> | `.research/sections/*9-1*/*` | ✅ Returns all files in matching dirs |
This catches slug variations like `Core-Concepts`, `core_concepts`, etc.
Used by `researcher` agent for path resolution:
| `.research/` directory missing | Auto-create on first write          |

content.value_statement: Research agents need consistent storage so drafts can reuse prior findings. This skill defines paths, naming rules, lookup steps, and templates for cached research files.
actual_capabilities: Provides normalization rules for chapter numbers, section numbers, and slugs.
Describes multi-tier lookup for existing section research files.
Provides templates for summary.md, sources.md, and research.md files.
Standardizes XML status outputs for research and directory resolution.
Explains when agents should read, write, or avoid cached research files.
limitations: It documents conventions; it does not run searches or verify source quality.
It expects agents to enforce path rules when reading or writing files.
It focuses on dokhak project structure and may need adaptation elsewhere.
It does not include executable storage tooling or validation scripts.

use_cases.title: Save Initial Research Cache
use_cases.description: Store topic summaries and source registries in the standard init research location.

use_cases.title: Reuse Section Findings
use_cases.description: Find existing section research across canonical and legacy directory names before collecting more data.

use_cases.title: Standardize Research Handoffs
use_cases.description: Use shared file templates and status formats so multiple agents can exchange research reliably.

prompt_templates.title: Save Init Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new topic cache.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the research-storage conventions to save topic research for {topic}. Create summary.md and sources.md under the init research directory.

prompt_templates.title: Create Section Research Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-storage to create research files for chapter {chapter}, section {section}, titled {title}. Follow the standard section templates.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Existing Research Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate lookup before collecting more research.
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve the research directory for chapter {chapter}, section {section}, and title {title}. Check canonical and legacy naming variations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Research Cache Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of stored research completeness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review cached research for {project}. Report missing subtopics, stale sources, and files that do not follow research-storage conventions.

output_examples.input: Save research for an init run about React performance.
output_examples.output: The agent creates a summary file and a sources file under the init research directory, then returns a saved confirmation.

output_examples.input: Find research for chapter 1, section 2, Core Concepts.
output_examples.output: The agent normalizes the chapter, section, and title. It checks canonical and legacy path variants before creating a new directory.

output_examples.input: Prepare section research for an incomplete topic.
output_examples.output: The agent adds missing subtopics to the section research file and updates the source registry with verified references.

best_practices: Normalize chapter, section, and title values before building paths.
Check existing research before collecting or writing new material.
Keep source registries current with verification dates and reliability notes.
anti_patterns: Do not write research files outside the documented research directories.
Do not skip legacy path lookup when reusing prior section research.
Do not store source links without reliability and verification context.

faq.question: What does this skill store?
faq.answer: It stores research summaries, source registries, and section research files in a consistent project structure.

faq.question: Does this skill perform web research?
faq.answer: No. It only defines where research results should be saved and how they should be formatted.

faq.question: Which agents should use it?
faq.answer: Research collectors, researchers, writers, and structure designers can use it for storage and lookup conventions.

faq.question: Can it read older directory names?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents a multi-tier lookup strategy for canonical and legacy section directory names.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown guide with examples, templates, and conventions.

faq.question: How should cached research be handled in Git?
faq.answer: The skill recommends ignoring regenerable research cache files when they should not be committed.
